चयनित सूची में सम्मिलित उम्मीदवारों को उनके ईमेल द्वारा सूचित करते हुए

1.  Job Title: Product Manager 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms. 

 
 
 
 
 
2. Job Title: Full Stack Developer 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Develop and enhance backend engines in Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.3 (Spring Data JPA / 
Hibernate, Spring Security + JWT), following the shared clean-architecture layering (api → 
application → domain → infrastructure), the standard { success, data } response envelope 
and the domain-exception pattern used across the fleet. 
2. Build and extend core engine capabilities — business objects (dynamic object types, fields 
and JSONB records with versioning and audit), dynamic forms, versioned workflows and 
tasks, rules / decision tables, documents, notifications, search, reporting, dashboards, 
scheduler and integrations — as configuration-driven features. 
3. Develop web services and REST APIs with auto-generated OpenAPI (SpringDoc) docs, and 
build typed, fail-closed inter-engine clients; respect database-per-engine ownership (no 
cross-engine database reads — consume curated, tenant-scoped HTTP datasets). 
4. Develop the web application in Next.js 16 / React 19 with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, 
Zustand, react-hook-form + zod and recharts — dynamic tenant-configured forms, 
workflow and case screens, dashboards and the per-engine service / API-client layer, 
serving all four actor classes. 
5. Implement and uphold tenant-scoped persistence: every query carries a bound tenant 
predicate, identifiers are allow-listed and never string-interpolated, and sensitive provider 
secrets are handled via the platform’s encrypted, fail-closed mechanisms. 
6. Author Flyway migrations for the production path and keep the entity model, 
repositories and schema consistent; use UUID identifiers and per-engine schemas per 
the established conventions. 
7. Integrate third-party and government services (SMS / email / SSO / payment / external 
APIs) through the integration engine with retry, circuit-breaker and data-transformation 
patterns; wire Redis caching and Apache Kafka event flows for cross-engine reactions 
(notifications, indexing, audit). 
8. Apply AI-assisted code review and technical enhancements; write unit and integration tests, 
participate in code reviews, and uphold secure-by-design and fail-closed coding practices. 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation, 
QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments. 

 
 
 
 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation, 
QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in full-stack web 
application development using Java / Spring Boot and React / Next.js. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong proficiency in Java 21, Spring Boot 3.3, Hibernate / JPA, Spring Security + JWT, 
and REST web-service development with OpenAPI. 
2. Proficiency in Next.js / React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind, Zustand and 
react-hook-form + zod. 
3. Solid working experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL 16), JSONB and GIN 
indexing, and version-control tools (Git). 
4. Understanding of microservice architecture and integration, multi-tenant isolation, 
clean / layered architecture, and configuration / metadata-driven design. 
5. Familiarity with Redis, Apache Kafka, Docker, and performance (JMeter / Gatling), 
functional, unit and integration testing. 
6. Awareness of W3C / GIGW and accessibility guidelines and of Agile delivery. 
Desirable Skill Set 
• Experience with workflow / BPM and rules engines (Camunda, Flowable, Drools). 
• Experience building dynamic form / metadata-driven systems and document / search 
/ notification subsystems. 
• Experience using AI-assisted development and code-review tools. 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms. 
 
 
 
 
3. Job Title: QA Tester 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated

/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Prepare the test strategy and test plans; design and execute functional, regression and 
integration test cases across all engines and the web application, mapped to acceptance 
criteria and requirement IDs. 
2. Design and execute the cross-tenant isolation test suite — a session for one tenant must 
never read, filter into, list or mutate another tenant’s data across any engine or API; treat 
any leak as a build-blocking defect. 
3. Test the dynamic configuration surface end -to-end: business object types and fields, 
dynamic forms (conditional visibility, calculated fields, validation), rules / decision 
tables, notification templates and dashboards — verifying that configuration, not 
code, drives behaviour. 
4. Test versioned-workflow execution and in-flight case migration: version immutability, 
cases pinning to their filed version, stage / task / action / transition correctness, SLA 
timers, clarification and escalation paths, and the always-valid START → END spine. 
5. Test authentication and authorization across the four actor classes and the RBAC / ABAC 
matrix; verify fail-closed behaviour (deny by default, honest "unavailable" responses). 
6. Test documents (upload, checksum, versioning), notifications (multi-channel dispatch 
and templates), search (relevance, highlighting, autocomplete), reporting and 
dashboards for correctness and tenant scoping. 
7. Own release testing and regression cycles across the ~20 engines; build automation with 
suitable API / UI frameworks and in-memory (H2) or containerised databases; support 
performance testing. 
8. Log, track and verify defects to closure using defect-tracking tools; maintain traceability 
from requirement to test to defect; support UAT and release sign-off. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance / 
testing of web and API-based systems. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong test design and execution across functional, regression, integration and release 
testing. 
2. REST API testing (Postman / REST-assured), test automation frameworks and E2E 
tools (Playwright or equivalent). 
3. Understanding of multi-tenant isolation testing, workflow / BPM testing and RBAC / 
authorization testing. 

 
 
Familiarity with PostgreSQL, bug-reporting / test-management tools, and CI-integrated test 
execution; awareness of performance-testing tools (JMeter/ Gatling). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms. 
 
 
 
 
4. Job Title: Application Security (AppSec) Specialist 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy 
(tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security 
filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing 
key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). 
2. Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application 
— covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token 
lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC / policy), input validation, injection prevention 
(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 4+ years of experience in DevOps / DevSecOps 
for microservice-based systems. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong hands-on Docker and Kubernetes; CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI / Jenkins / 
GitHub Actions) with integrated security scanning, on self-hosted runners and 
registries. 
Secrets management, Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform / Ansible), and release-
management discipline (Flyway-based change control, promotion, rollback). 
Experience operating Apache Kafka and Redis and deploying Spring Boot + Next.js workloads 
on sovereign 
/ government cloud. 
Observability stacks (Prometheus / Grafana / ELK) and build-time security tooling.

6. Job Title: Platform & Security Engineer 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Design and operate the hosting-agnostic environment on private / sovereign / 
government cloud: compute, network topology and segmentation, firewalls, TLS / 
ingress, DNS and strict environment separation (dev / staging / production). 
2. Operate the self-managed data and messaging estate at fleet scale — PostgreSQL 16 with 
HA / streaming replication (one database per engine), Redis (Sentinel / Cluster) and a 
multi-broker Apache Kafka cluster — with capacity planning, tuning and growth 
headroom for ~20 services. 
3. Own platform availability (target uptime, health management, self-healing), 
monitoring, alerting and capacity management across the fleet; ensure the append-only 
audit store and its immutability triggers are protected and backed up. 
4. Own backup and disaster-recovery architecture and rehearsed restore drills; define and 
prove RPO / RTO targets and maintain the DR runbook. 
5. Own platform -layer and infrastructure security — hardening, network policy, least -
privilege access, and the custody, storage and rotation of the platform -admin signing  
key, internal-service key and encryption keys (separated from the runtime application). 
6. Define and enforce the production topology and scaling model (replicas for IAM / 
workflow / business-object and other high-load engines) and partner with DevSecOps on 
deployment and with AppSec on end-to-end hardening and audit evidence. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 6+ years of experience in infrastructure / 
platform engineering with a strong security focus; experience operating production 
microservice fleets preferred. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Hosting-agnostic experience on private / sovereign / government cloud (VMware, 
OpenStack or KVM) and Kubernetes — without dependence on public-hyperscaler 
managed services. 
2. Deep self-managed PostgreSQL (HA, streaming replication, many databases); Redis 
and Apache Kafka operations; strong Linux and networking. 
3. Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform / Ansible), backup / DR tooling, and self-
hosted observability (Prometheus / Grafana / ELK). 
4. Key-management and secrets custody; familiarity with STQC / DPDP infrastructure 
controls and data-residency requirements.

Job Description

workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

6. Author Flyway migrations for the production path and keep the entity model, 
repositories and schema consistent; use UUID identifiers and per-engine schemas per 
the established conventions. 
7. Integrate third-party and government services (SMS / email / SSO / payment / external 
APIs) through the integration engine with retry, circuit-breaker and data-transformation 
patterns; wire Redis caching and Apache Kafka event flows for cross-engine reactions 
(notifications, indexing, audit). 
8. Apply AI-assisted code review and technical enhancements; write unit and integration tests, 
participate in code reviews, and uphold secure-by-design and fail-closed coding practices.

QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments.

fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes.

mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

6. Author Flyway migrations for the production path and keep the entity model, 
repositories and schema consistent; use UUID identifiers and per-engine schemas per 
the established conventions. 
7. Integrate third-party and government services (SMS / email / SSO / payment / external 
APIs) through the integration engine with retry, circuit-breaker and data-transformation 
patterns; wire Redis caching and Apache Kafka event flows for cross-engine reactions

8. Apply AI-assisted code review and technical enhancements; write unit and integration tests, 
participate in code reviews, and uphold secure-by-design and fail-closed coding practices.

QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments.

No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy 
(tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security 
filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing 
key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). 
2. Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application 
— covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token 
lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC / policy), input validation, injection prevention 
(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration:

The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Prepare the test strategy and test plans; design and execute functional, regression and 
integration test cases across all engines and the web application, mapped to acceptance 
criteria and requirement IDs. 
2. Design and execute the cross-tenant isolation test suite — a session for one tenant must 
never read, filter into, list or mutate another tenant’s data across any engine or API; treat 
any leak as a build-blocking defect. 
3. Test the dynamic configuration surface end -to-end: business object types and fields, 
dynamic forms (conditional visibility, calculated fields, validation), rules / decision 
tables, notification templates and dashboards — verifying that configuration, not 
code, drives behaviour. 
4. Test versioned-workflow execution and in-flight case migration: version immutability, 
cases pinning to their filed version, stage / task / action / transition correctness, SLA 
timers, clarification and escalation paths, and the always-valid START → END spine. 
5. Test authentication and authorization across the four actor classes and the RBAC / ABAC 
matrix; verify fail-closed behaviour (deny by default, honest "unavailable" responses). 
6. Test documents (upload, checksum, versioning), notifications (multi-channel dispatch 
and templates), search (relevance, highlighting, autocomplete), reporting and 
dashboards for correctness and tenant scoping. 
7. Own release testing and regression cycles across the ~20 engines; build automation with 
suitable API / UI frameworks and in-memory (H2) or containerised databases; support 
performance testing. 
8. Log, track and verify defects to closure using defect-tracking tools; maintain traceability 
from requirement to test to defect; support UAT and release sign-off. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance / 
testing of web and API-based systems. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong test design and execution across functional, regression, integration and release 
testing. 
2. REST API testing (Postman / REST-assured), test automation frameworks and E2E 
tools (Playwright or equivalent). 
3. Understanding of multi-tenant isolation testing, workflow / BPM testing and RBAC / 
authorization testing. 

 
 
Familiarity with PostgreSQL, bug-reporting / test-management tools, and CI-integrated test 
execution; awareness of performance-testing tools (JMeter/ Gatling).

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

Job Description

Role and Responsibilities 
1. Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy 
(tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security 
filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing 
key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). 
2. Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application 
— covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token 
lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC / policy), input validation, injection prevention 
(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management).

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

1.  Job Title: Product Manager 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

Job Description

/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Develop and enhance backend engines in Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.3 (Spring Data JPA / 
Hibernate, Spring Security + JWT), following the shared clean-architecture layering (api → 
application → domain → infrastructure), the standard { success, data } response envelope 
and the domain-exception pattern used across the fleet. 
2. Build and extend core engine capabilities — business objects (dynamic object types, fields 
and JSONB records with versioning and audit), dynamic forms, versioned workflows and 
tasks, rules / decision tables, documents, notifications, search, reporting, dashboards, 
scheduler and integrations — as configuration-driven features. 
3. Develop web services and REST APIs with auto-generated OpenAPI (SpringDoc) docs, and 
build typed, fail-closed inter-engine clients; respect database-per-engine ownership (no 
cross-engine database reads — consume curated, tenant-scoped HTTP datasets). 
4. Develop the web application in Next.js 16 / React 19 with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, 
Zustand, react-hook-form + zod and recharts — dynamic tenant-configured forms, 
workflow and case screens, dashboards and the per-engine service / API-client layer, 
serving all four actor classes. 
5. Implement and uphold tenant-scoped persistence: every query carries a bound tenant 
predicate, identifiers are allow-listed and never string-interpolated, and sensitive provider 
secrets are handled via the platform’s encrypted, fail-closed mechanisms. 
6. Author Flyway migrations for the production path and keep the entity model, 
repositories and schema consistent; use UUID identifiers and per-engine schemas per 
the established conventions. 
7. Integrate third-party and government services (SMS / email / SSO / payment / external 
APIs) through the integration engine with retry, circuit-breaker and data-transformation 
patterns; wire Redis caching and Apache Kafka event flows for cross-engine reactions 
(notifications, indexing, audit). 
8. Apply AI-assisted code review and technical enhancements; write unit and integration tests, 
participate in code reviews, and uphold secure-by-design and fail-closed coding practices. 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation, 
QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments. 

 
 
 
 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation, 
QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in full-stack web 
application development using Java / Spring Boot and React / Next.js. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong proficiency in Java 21, Spring Boot 3.3, Hibernate / JPA, Spring Security + JWT, 
and REST web-service development with OpenAPI. 
2. Proficiency in Next.js / React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind, Zustand and 
react-hook-form + zod. 
3. Solid working experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL 16), JSONB and GIN 
indexing, and version-control tools (Git). 
4. Understanding of microservice architecture and integration, multi-tenant isolation, 
clean / layered architecture, and configuration / metadata-driven design. 
5. Familiarity with Redis, Apache Kafka, Docker, and performance (JMeter / Gatling), 
functional, unit and integration testing. 
6. Awareness of W3C / GIGW and accessibility guidelines and of Agile delivery. 
Desirable Skill Set 
• Experience with workflow / BPM and rules engines (Camunda, Flowable, Drools). 
• Experience building dynamic form / metadata-driven systems and document / search 
/ notification subsystems.

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

criteria and requirement IDs. 
2. Design and execute the cross-tenant isolation test suite — a session for one tenant must 
never read, filter into, list or mutate another tenant’s data across any engine or API; treat

3. Test the dynamic configuration surface end -to-end: business object types and fields,

code, drives behaviour.

5. Test authentication and authorization across the four actor classes and the RBAC / ABAC 
matrix; verify fail-closed behaviour (deny by default, honest "unavailable" responses). 
6. Test documents (upload, checksum, versioning), notifications (multi-channel dispatch 
and templates), search (relevance, highlighting, autocomplete), reporting and 
dashboards for correctness and tenant scoping. 
7. Own release testing and regression cycles across the ~20 engines; build automation with 
suitable API / UI frameworks and in-memory (H2) or containerised databases; support 
performance testing. 
8. Log, track and verify defects to closure using defect-tracking tools; maintain traceability 
from requirement to test to defect; support UAT and release sign-off. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance / 
testing of web and API-based systems. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong test design and execution across functional, regression, integration and release 
testing. 
2. REST API testing (Postman / REST-assured), test automation frameworks and E2E 
tools (Playwright or equivalent). 
3. Understanding of multi-tenant isolation testing, workflow / BPM testing and RBAC / 
authorization testing. 

 
 
Familiarity with PostgreSQL, bug-reporting / test-management tools, and CI-integrated test 
execution; awareness of performance-testing tools (JMeter/ Gatling).

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms. 
 
 
 
 
4. Job Title: Application Security (AppSec) Specialist 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy 
(tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security 
filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing 
key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). 
2. Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application 
— covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token 
lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC / policy), input validation, injection prevention 
(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent

behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign

workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence).

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes.

5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events.

1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development.

SCA tooling.

Openings Details Digital India Corporation is inviting applications for the position of Application Security (AppSec) Specialist on a contractual basis. Position Application Security (AppSec) Specialist No. of Positions 01 Last Date 18th November 2026 Responsibilities Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy (tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application — covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC/policy), input validation, injection prevention (allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at rest) — and drive remediation to closure. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the fleet and the web / API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls — and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government security audit, and support incident response for security events. 1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields,

3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides.

product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred.

platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows.

token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows.

security audit, and support incident response for security events.

secure software development.

security, and session / credential security.

and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management).

1.  Job Title: Product Manager 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle

Role and Responsibilities 
1. Threat-model the platform end-to-end and review the secure design of multi-tenancy 
(tenant_id isolation and bound tenant predicates), the deny-by-default / fail-closed security 
filters, and the separated three- key trust model (fleet JWT secret, platform-admin signing 
key, internal-service key — kept distinct and never merged). 
2. Conduct secure code reviews across the Java / Spring engines and the Next.js application 
— covering authentication (BCrypt password hashing, lockout, session limits, token 
lifecycle), authorization (RBAC / ABAC / policy), input validation, injection prevention 
(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

1.  Job Title: Product Manager 
No. of Posts: 1 
Job Description 
 
About the Platform 
The Digital Office Platform is a multi-tenant, configuration-driven government case-management 
platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle 
— data model, intake forms, versioned workflows, roles, SLAs, notifications, audit and reporting 
— and run real cases end-to-end without custom code per tenant. It is built as ~20 independent 
Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated 
behind a Next.js web application, and deployed hosting-agnostic on sovereign 
/ government cloud using open-source components. Tenant isolation is by tenant_id; published 
workflow versions are immutable and live cases pin to their version; security and data 
boundaries fail closed. 
Role and Responsibilities 
1. Elicit, analyse and document requirements for each onboarding government body; prepare 
the BRD / FRD with unique requirement IDs, acceptance criteria and a requirement 
traceability matrix linking every requirement to a design element and a test case. 
2. Translate each body’s case lifecycle into configuration — business object types and fields, 
dynamic intake forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields), 
versioned workflows (stages, tasks, actions, transitions), roles / personas, rules / decision 
tables, SLAs, notification templates and dashboards 
— so a new office is stood up by configuration, not code. 
3. Define the workflow -versioning and in -flight case-migration policy: published versions are 
immutable, live cases pin to the version in force when filed, and any migration between 
versions is explicit, mapped stage-to-stage and audited. 
4. Specify SLA, clarification, escalation and reminder rules, and the notification matrix 
(EMAIL / SMS / WhatsApp / push / in-app / webhook) per workflow stage and actor 
class. 
5. Specify role-based access needs across the four actor classes — platform admin, tenant 
staff, citizens / applicants, and second parties / respondents — and the RBAC / ABAC / 
policy model with the IAM owner. 
6. Define reporting and dashboard requirements as curated, tenant-scoped datasets and 
named metrics (never ad-hoc cross-tenant SQL), and the KPIs each role needs. 
7. Own the product roadmap, MoSCoW prioritisation, release phasing and scope discipline 
across the ~20 engines; chair backlog grooming and sprint planning. 
8. Coordinate stakeholders across government bodies, DIC and the platform team; plan 
and drive UAT, capture sign-off, and manage change requests through a controlled 
process. 
9. Author and maintain product documentation — user manuals per actor class, 
configuration playbooks, release notes and onboarding guides. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in business analysis / 
product management for enterprise or government IT systems; experience with case-
management, grievance-redressal or workflow platforms preferred. 

 
 
 
 
 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong requirements engineering and documentation (requirement specifications, 
manuals, traceability) and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical 
audiences. 
2. Business-process and workflow modelling (BPMN an advantage); ability to express 
case lifecycles as configuration rather than code. 
3. Working understanding of multi-tenant SaaS, metadata / configuration-driven 
platforms, RBAC / ABAC, SLA design and notification workflows. 
4. Knowledge of GIGW, accessibility and DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance as 
they affect requirements. 
5. Comfortable reading REST API contracts, data models and configuration schemas; 
proficient with Agile tooling (Jira / Confluence). 
 
Consolidated Remuneration: 
 
1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within 
the approved project norms.

Role and Responsibilities 
1. Develop and enhance backend engines in Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.3 (Spring Data JPA / 
Hibernate, Spring Security + JWT), following the shared clean-architecture layering (api → 
application → domain → infrastructure), the standard { success, data } response envelope 
and the domain-exception pattern used across the fleet. 
2. Build and extend core engine capabilities — business objects (dynamic object types, fields 
and JSONB records with versioning and audit), dynamic forms, versioned workflows and 
tasks, rules / decision tables, documents, notifications, search, reporting, dashboards, 
scheduler and integrations — as configuration-driven features. 
3. Develop web services and REST APIs with auto-generated OpenAPI (SpringDoc) docs, and

5. Implement and uphold tenant-scoped persistence: every query carries a bound tenant 
predicate, identifiers are allow-listed and never string-interpolated, and sensitive provider 
secrets are handled via the platform’s encrypted, fail-closed mechanisms. 
6. Author Flyway migrations for the production path and keep the entity model, 
repositories and schema consistent; use UUID identifiers and per-engine schemas per 
the established conventions. 
7. Integrate third-party and government services (SMS / email / SSO / payment / external 
APIs) through the integration engine with retry, circuit-breaker and data-transformation 
patterns; wire Redis caching and Apache Kafka event flows for cross-engine reactions 
(notifications, indexing, audit). 
8. Apply AI-assisted code review and technical enhancements; write unit and integration tests, 
participate in code reviews, and uphold secure-by-design and fail-closed coding practices. 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation, 
QA support, source control, maintenance and deployments. 

 
 
 
 
9. Work across the complete SDLC — functional and technical specifications, documentation,

react-hook-form + zod. 
3. Solid working experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL 16), JSONB and GIN 
indexing, and version-control tools (Git). 
4. Understanding of microservice architecture and integration, multi-tenant isolation, 
clean / layered architecture, and configuration / metadata-driven design. 
5. Familiarity with Redis, Apache Kafka, Docker, and performance (JMeter / Gatling), 
functional, unit and integration testing. 
6. Awareness of W3C / GIGW and accessibility guidelines and of Agile delivery.

2. Design and execute the cross-tenant isolation test suite — a session for one tenant must

6. Test documents (upload, checksum, versioning), notifications (multi-channel dispatch

dashboards for correctness and tenant scoping. 
7. Own release testing and regression cycles across the ~20 engines; build automation with 
suitable API / UI frameworks and in-memory (H2) or containerised databases; support 
performance testing. 
8. Log, track and verify defects to closure using defect-tracking tools; maintain traceability

1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance / 
testing of web and API-based systems. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong test design and execution across functional, regression, integration and release 
testing. 
2. REST API testing (Postman / REST-assured), test automation frameworks and E2E 
tools (Playwright or equivalent). 
3. Understanding of multi-tenant isolation testing, workflow / BPM testing and RBAC / 
authorization testing. 

 
 
Familiarity with PostgreSQL, bug-reporting / test-management tools, and CI-integrated test

(allow-listed identifiers, parameterised queries) and secret handling (AES-256-GCM at 
rest) — and drive remediation to closure. 
3. Plan and coordinate VAPT / penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across the 
fleet and the web 
/ API surface; triage SAST / DAST / SCA findings, assign severities and track fixes. 
4. Own DPDP (Act 2023 / Rules 2025) compliance review — data-flow and data-inventory 
mapping, consent, retention, data-minimisation and cross-tenant data-isolation controls 
— and the immutable audit trail (append-only store, SHA-256 integrity, field-level diff). 
5. Review and advise on the documented residual hardening items (e.g. RS256 / JWKS 
token hardening and token revocation, platform MFA) and verify closure as they are 
addressed; define the secure-coding and security-testing standards the team follows. 
6. Prepare security evidence and documentation for STQC clearance and government 
security audit, and support incident response for security events. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 5+ years of experience in application security / 
secure software development. 

 
 
Required Skill Set 
Strong knowledge of OWASP Top 10, secure coding in Java / Spring, JWT / token 
security, and session / credential security. 
Experience in multi-tenant data-isolation review and in handling web / API security audits 
and their tools. 
Experience planning and coordinating VAPT / penetration testing and using SAST / DAST / 
SCA tooling. 
Working knowledge of DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025, GIGW and STQC requirements, and 
of cryptographic controls (hashing, authenticated encryption, key management).

1. Consolidated remuneration shall be commensurate with qualifications and experience within

government bodies, DIC and the engineering team.

delivery management.

coordination.

sufficient to coordinate development, support and provisioning.

11. Job Title: Frontend Developer

Job Description

platform that lets many independent government bodies each configure their own case lifecycle

Spring Boot microservices (engines), each owning its own PostgreSQL database, coordinated

Role and Responsibilities 
1. Develop and maintain the platform’s web application in Next.js 16 / React 19 with 
TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Zustand and react-hook-form + zod, delivering responsive, 
accessible interfaces for all four actor classes (platform admin, tenant staff, citizens / 
applicants and second parties / respondents). 
2. Build the dynamic, configuration-driven UI — render tenant-configured object types and 
forms (sections, rows, columns, conditional visibility, calculated fields, validation) from 
metadata, so new forms and fields appear without front-end code changes. 
3. Implement workflow and case screens — stage / task / action views, transitions, SLA and 
status indicators, clarification and escalation flows — driven by the versioned -workflow 
configuration. 
4. Build dashboards and reports in the UI using charting libraries (e.g. recharts), consuming 
curated, tenant-scoped datasets exposed by the engines. 
5. Develop and maintain the per -engine service / API -client layer that consumes the REST 
APIs, handling the standard { success, data } response envelope, authentication / JWT 
tokens and fail-closed error states. 
6. Ensure accessibility (GIGW / WCAG) and cross-browser, mobile-first responsiveness; 
optimise front-end performance (code-splitting, lazy loading, caching). 
7. Collaborate with the UI/UX design, backend and QA teams to translate wireframes and 
requirements into functional features; write unit and component tests and participate in 
code reviews. 
Qualifications and Experiences 
1. Bachelor's degree in any discipline with 3+ years of experience in front-end web application 
development using React / Next.js. 
Required Skill Set 
1. Strong proficiency in JavaScript and TypeScript, and in React / Next.js, HTML and CSS. 
2. Experience with state management (Zustand / Redux or similar), form libraries 
(react-hook-form) and schema validation (zod). 
3. Proficiency with Tailwind CSS or equivalent, responsive / mobile-first design and 
component-based architecture. 
4. Experience consuming REST APIs and handling authentication, tokens and error / 
loading states; version-control tools (Git). 
5. Understanding of W3C / GIGW and accessibility (WCAG) guidelines and of Agile delivery. 

 
 
Desirable Skill Set 
Experience building dynamic / metadata-driven forms and configurable UI. 
Familiarity with charting / data-visualisation libraries and dashboard development. 
Awareness of multi-tenant front-end concerns and of AI-assisted development tools.
